TextBlock.Text: Falklands War 1982 - Britain
Your command
Lead the British Task Force from South Georgia to the final operations off Stanley. Your ships, submarines and aircraft form a persistent force across connected missions.

'Historical Reinforcements' game mode will deliver historically-correct reinforcement waves at each stage of the campaign. `Points-based` mode will allow you to create your own forces using the Task Force Builder. Note that the Task Force Builder itself is generally restricted to the historically-available units in the theater. If you want to play the campaign with any unit in the game, restart and choose 'Unrestricted' mode.'
Force flagship

Your force has one overall flagship. In Historical Reinforcements mode this is HMS Hermes, locked when she joins the campaign. HMS Invincible is a supporting carrier and her loss alone does not end the campaign.

In Points Based mode, including Unrestricted, use Assign flagship on any owned surface ship to transfer command. A flagship is assigned automatically when your first surface ships join. Moving ships between groups or Reserve does not change the designation.

Whenever the flagship deploys, it must survive. Its loss ends the campaign, even when returning from a failed mission. Missions before Hermes arrives and detachments without the flagship can proceed normally. Formation leaders do not carry this survival requirement.
Before each operation
Read the mission briefing, check the required forces, and assign suitable task forces to the deployment zones. Check aircraft assignments and remaining weapons before launching.
Read the resupply notice before committing to the next operation. Repair and rearm are available only at designated stages.
Plan for the whole campaign
Losses, damage, ammunition expenditure and surviving crews affect later operations. Preserve scarce aircraft and specialist ships.

Optional missions have limited windows, and advancing the main campaign can close and skip an unfinished side mission. Save regularly, especially before advancing. Note: replaying missions for a better result is not allowed in this campaign!
Reinforcements and Task Forces
Historical Reinforcements
Ships, submarines and aircraft arrive in reinforcement packages as the campaign advances. Packages may arrive as formed task groups or as individual units in Reserve.
This mode does not use campaign points to purchase units. Replacement forces depend on the campaign's reinforcement schedule.
Points Based
Use Task Force Builder to buy units from the roster available for the selected mission. Purchases spend campaign points and must respect the force cap and mission requirements.
Mission completion can award additional points and increase the force cap. Difficulty changes starting resources, rewards, repair costs and whether purchased ships include their aircraft.
Check the aircraft included with each purchase. Helicopters cost points but do not consume the fleet cap. There is no national purchase discount in this campaign.
Task forces and Reserve
Organise your force into separate task groups and move units between groups and Reserve as required. Reserve is a holding pool, not an additional deployed task group.
Each mission sets its own limits on ships, submarines and task forces. Deployment zones can restrict ship types and require a carrier or another specific role.
Aircraft and Submarine Operations
Embarked aircraft
Assign aircraft to compatible ships and check hangar capacity before deployment. Aircraft availability and losses carry forward with the campaign force.
Use the Starting Airborne Flights options offered by the selected mission to prepare eligible flights. Each flight must satisfy its aircraft-type and role restrictions.
Land-based aircraft
Airbases hold finite aircraft inventories. RAF Wideawake supports eligible long-range operations, including the Vulcan flight offered for Black Buck missions.
A shore-based aircraft is not a replacement for an embarked aircraft unless it can be assigned to a compatible ship. Check the mission's available flights and bases.
Optional submarine operations
Submarine missions use their own deployment requirements. Completing them will alter later operations.
Keeping the Task Force in Action
Repair and rearm

Repair and rearm facilities are only available to the British Task Force when moving away from the islands to the replenishment zone. Missions will tell you if rearm and repair is available after the mission.
Light and moderate damage can be repaired when facilities are available. Heavy damage cannot be repaired by the force's at-sea facilities.
Repairs cost campaign points in Points Based mode. Eligible repairs are free in Historical Reinforcements mode. Difficulty modifies repair costs in Points Based mode.
Rearm is free at the designated stages and happens automatically. Conserve ammunition between replenishment opportunities and check each ship before deployment.
Losses and replacements

A ship lost in combat provides no points refund. In Points Based mode, dismissing a unit or decommissioning a heavily damaged unit returns only part of its value, according to the selected difficulty.
Reinforcements and newly available purchases do not restore aircraft already lost. Check both the surviving air group and the next mission's requirements.
Rescue and experience
Recover survivors with suitable ships or helicopters when conditions permit. In Points Based mode, every 10 survivors rescued earns one campaign point at mission end.
Crews improve their proficiency by surviving missions. Keeping experienced units in action strengthens the force for later operations.
Commander and Campaign Awards
Royal Navy command
The campaign begins with a Royal Navy rear admiral, with Sandy Woodward as the default commander. The Service Record tracks campaign progress, combat results, losses and rescues.
South Atlantic Medal with Rosette

Completing Operation Paraquet unlocks the South Atlantic Medal with Rosette in your Service Record. This is an early acknowledgement of qualifying campaign service, recorded retrospectively as a 1982 award.
The rosette denotes qualifying operational service. The medal is awarded once and is not a gallantry decoration.
Order of the Bath
Completing The Final Approach unlocks appointment as a Knight Commander of the Order of the Bath (KCB). The award record is dated 11 October 1982, reflecting the post-war honours.
This campaign award follows the historical honour received by Rear Admiral Woodward. For a custom commander it represents equivalent achievement in command of the campaign.
Reading your awards
Select a ribbon in the Service Record to read its award record.
Unit Prices
Reference prices for the campaign roster. Actual purchase availability depends on the selected mission and acquisition setting. Select a class name to open its unit reference.
